name: Ogunyemi Samuel Ayomide
positioning: I ship complete, working products: from the PRD to the database to the deployed app.
story:
I'm Ayomide, also known as Tubayox: a Computer Science student at the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) in Nigeria. I build full-stack web products and applied machine learning systems, and I care about finishing them: writing the PRD, designing the schema, building the interface and deploying something real people can use.

So far that means a live portfolio site for a photographer with its own admin dashboard, a ticketing platform that is in active development, a product-design case study for football e-ticketing, and my final-year project: a machine learning system that predicts student dropout risk.

I have also held leadership roles: Faculty President of the School of Computing, and Chairman of the ACOMS Electoral Committee. They are where I practise the part of shipping that is not code: process, fairness, deadlines and people.

howIWork.title: Start from the PRD
howIWork.text: I write down who the product is for, the rules it must enforce and what ships in which phase before I write code. The football e-ticketing PRD and its 12-week plan came first, and the build follows from them.

howIWork.title: Enforce rules where they cannot be bypassed
howIWork.text: In ArenaPass, roles are checked in middleware for a good experience and again in Postgres Row Level Security, so a bug in a page cannot leak data.

howIWork.title: Measure before claiming
howIWork.text: I moved the photographer's database closer to its servers and measured page render from Lagos before and after. On the ML project I state that the headline results are on augmented data.

howIWork.title: Ship, then harden
howIWork.text: Real users find real problems. After launch I tightened the admin: strong secrets required, shared rate limits and session invalidation on password change.
